topic: Gulbrandsen complex conductor Fresnel dip vs Schlick metal whitewash rig
topic_zh: Gulbrandsen 复折射率金属伪布儒斯特暗边凹陷对比朴素 Schlick 单调泛白
scope: Deterministic Ole Gulbrandsen (JCGT 2014 / MaterialX artistic_ior / OpenPBR) complex conductor Fresnel reflectance (F_cond(mu) = ((eta - mu)^2 + kappa^2) / ((eta + mu)^2 + kappa^2) with eta = 0.30, kappa = 0.40, F0 = 0.3514, Pseudo-Brewster minimum at mu = sqrt(eta^2 + kappa^2) = 0.5000 / 60 deg) versus naive monotonic dielectric Schlick (F0 + (1 - F0)*(1 - mu)^5) and 64-polarization wave-impedance quadrature across 17 incident viewing angles (theta_i in [0 deg, 80 deg]).

protocol.function: F_cond(μ) = ((η − μ)² + κ²) / ((η + μ)² + κ²) → 60° Dip = 0.2500 vs Monotonic Schlick 0.3716 (+48.65% Whitewash)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 incident viewing angles capture the exact Pseudo-Brewster conductor dip without grazing whitewash

good_fit: Gold, copper, brass, aluminum, and chrome metals in MaterialX artistic_ior, OpenPBR, Arnold, and Three.js
Preserving the Pseudo-Brewster reflectance dip at cos(theta_B) = sqrt(eta^2 + kappa^2) (60° dip to 0.2500)
Eliminating the +48.65% chalky edge whitewash of monotonic dielectric Schlick approximations on metals
Evaluating exact complex-IOR reflectance in 5 scalar operations without complex square roots
not_for: Pure dielectrics with zero extinction (kappa == 0) such as water or glass where standard Schlick is accurate
Unlit matte clay or diffuse chalk
Multi-layer thin-film interference coatings (use Belcour-Barla Iridescence Round 102)
